description: Beryllium is a chemical element with symbol Be and atomic number 4. It is a steel-gray, hard, strong, lightweight and brittle alkaline earth metal that occurs naturally only in combination with other elements to form minerals. It is relatively rare in the universe, usually occurring as a product of the spallation of larger atomic nuclei that have collided with cosmic rays.
uses: In structural applications, beryllium is used for aircraft components, missiles, spacecraft, and satellites due to its high flexural rigidity, thermal stability, and low density. It is the most common window material for X-ray equipment and particle detectors because of its transparency to X-rays and ionizing radiation. When added as an alloying element to aluminum, copper, iron, or nickel, beryllium improves physical properties, and beryllium copper alloys are used to make tools and components that are strong and do not create sparks.
characteristics: Beryllium is steel gray and brittle at room temperature with a close-packed hexagonal crystal structure and exceptional stiffness (Young's modulus 287 GPa). It has a melting point of 1287 °C and a low density of 1.85 times that of water, with the highest sound conduction speed among metals at about 12.9 km/s. It dissipates the most heat per unit weight among all metals and has a relatively low coefficient of linear thermal expansion, making it uniquely stable under extreme temperature differences.
